sentiment.label: risk_off
sentiment.reason_it: Il sentiment di mercato è risk-off a causa dell'aumento del VIX del 39.68% e della chiusura negativa dei mercati azionari nella sessione precedente. Il DXY è salito dello 0.66%, mentre il TLT è sceso dello 0.51%. L'aumento della volatilità e la debolezza dei mercati azionari contribuiscono a questo sentiment.
sentiment.reason_en: Market sentiment is risk-off due to the 39.68% increase in VIX and the negative close of equity markets in the previous session. The DXY rose 0.66%, while TLT fell 0.51%. The increase in volatility and weakness in equity markets contribute to this sentiment.

market_impact_summary.it: Nella sessione precedente, i mercati azionari hanno chiuso in negativo, con S&P 500 -2.64% e STOXX 600 -0.40%. Il VIX è salito a 21.51, aumentando del 39.68%. Il DXY è salito dello 0.66%, mentre il TLT è sceso dello 0.51%. Le materie prime sono state deboli, con il petrolio in calo del 2.04% e l'oro in calo del 2.47%.
market_impact_summary.en: In the previous session, equity markets closed lower, with S&P 500 -2.64% and STOXX 600 -0.40%. VIX rose to 21.51, up 39.68%. The DXY rose 0.66%, while TLT fell 0.51%. Commodities were weak, with oil down 2.04% and gold down 2.47%.

audio_script_it:
Buongiorno, benvenuti al Morning Briefing di Price Alert.

I mercati asiatici hanno chiuso in rosso. Il Nikkei ha perso l'1.31%, Shanghai lo 0.74%.

Mentre le borse mondiali osservano la consueta pausa festiva, i riflettori restano accesi sui mercati che non dormono mai. Nella seduta precedente, S&P 500 in calo del 2.64%, VIX in rialzo del 39.68%, segnale di crescente avversione al rischio. L'oro è sceso del 2.47% a $4365.3/oncia, il petrolio Brent in calo del 2.04% a $93.09 Il Dollar Index ha guadagnato lo 0.66%, mentre l'EUR/USD è sceso dello 0.73% a 1.15 Il rendimento del decennale USA è salito dell'1.32% al 4.53%.

Sul fronte geopolitico, si segnalano le tensioni in Ucraina e le preoccupazioni sull'impatto economico delle riforme in Europa. Inoltre, la crisi nello stretto di Hormuz evidenzia le strategie energetiche dei principali attori globali.

Nessun dato macro rilevante in uscita oggi, in quanto i mercati sono chiusi per il fine settimana.

Passiamo ora al comparto degli asset digitali. Bitcoin si mantiene sopra i sessantamila dollari, con una variazione del 2,13% a 62.622 dollari. Tuttavia, i flussi ETF hanno registrato una significativa uscita di 325,7 milioni di dollari. Questo movimento potrebbe essere influenzato da una serie di fattori, tra cui la recente performance del mercato crypto.

Anche le principali altcoin mostrano movimenti positivi: Ethereum guadagna il 2,27% a mille 621 dollari, Solana sale del 2,72% a 65 dollari e BNB aumenta dell'1,90% a 593 dollari.

Il Fear & Greed Index è a 12, nella zona di Extreme Fear, suggerisce cautela tra gli investitori.

Nessun dato macro in agenda oggi. Per approfondire i temi di oggi, sulla nostra piattaforma trovate gli articoli completi nella sezione Storie in Primo Piano. Grazie per l'attenzione e a domani.
audio_script_en: Good morning, welcome to the Price Alert Morning Briefing. Asian markets closed in the red. Nikkei lost 1.31%, Shanghai 0.74%. While global stock markets are observing the usual festive pause, the spotlight remains on the markets that never sleep. In the previous session, S&P 500 down 2.64%, VIX up 39.68%, a sign of growing risk aversion. Gold fell 2.47% to $4,365.3/oz, Brent crude oil down 2.04% to $93.09 The Dollar Index gained 0.66%, while EUR/USD fell 0.73% to 1.15 The 10-year US yield rose 1.32% to 4.53%. On the geopolitical front, tensions in Ukraine and concerns about the economic impact of reforms in Europe are reported. Furthermore, the crisis in the Strait of Hormuz highlights the energy strategies of major global players. No major macroeconomic data out today, as markets are closed for the weekend. Let's pivot to the cryptocurrency markets. Bitcoin remains above sixty thousand dollars, with a variation of 2.13% to $62,622 However, ETF flows have recorded a significant outflow of $325.7 million. This movement could be influenced by a series of factors, including the recent crypto market performance. Major altcoins also show positive movements: Ethereum gains 2.27% to $1,621, Solana rises 2.72% to $65, and BNB increases 1.9% to $593 The Fear & Greed Index is at 12, in the Extreme Fear zone, suggesting caution among investors. No macroeconomic data on the agenda today. To delve deeper into today's topics, find the full articles in the Top Stories section on our platform. Thank you for your attention, and see you tomorrow.

articles.title: Ukraine's fiscal and financial challenges
articles.snippet: As it faces the exigencies of an existential war, Ukraine is confronted with stark fiscal and financial policy trade-offs, despite the mitigation provided by large-scale external financial support. So far, its authorities have kept monetary and financial stability under control beyond a relatively brief initial episode of turmoil in 2022. What is the broad fiscal equation for Ukraine looking forward, taking into account uncertainties about European funding beyond 2027? Can domestic revenue be raised? This event explores the path toward a new European social contract, one centered on renewed economic strategy, resilience, solidarity,…

articles.title: Oil Market Flying Blind as Dark Tanker Traffic Surges in Hormuz
articles.snippet: Tanker traffic through the Strait of Hormuz has collapsed by 90% to 95% compared to pre-war levels, analysts concur. Some oil cargoes continue to trickle through the critical chokepoint, but under increasingly opaque operating conditions, complicating the tracking of oil and gas flows and obscuring the visibility of how much energy supply actually reaches buyers these days. Traffic appears to have ramped up in recent weeks, according to an analysis of shipping data by Reuters energy columnist Ron Bousso. More vessels are leaving the region after…

articles.title: AI Boom or Political Play? Trump Channels Defense Funds Into Dying Coal Plants
articles.snippet: The Trump administration is set to channel nearly $700 million in federal funds into the U.S. coal industry Thursday, invoking a Korean War-era statute to prop up existing power plants, finance new construction, and push open a California export terminal that has been blocked for nearly two decades. The centerpiece is $425 million distributed under the Defense Production Act to 13 existing coal plants across West Virginia, Kentucky, North Carolina, Indiana, Tennessee, Arkansas, Arizona, Oklahoma, North Dakota, and Wisconsin.
